newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Spanish win Brazil's first gas firm sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spanish win Brazil's first gas firm sale.

text.p: A Spanish-led consortium snatched up a controling stake in Rio de Janeiro state gas company CEG and piped gas distributor Riogas for 622.2 million reais in the first privatization of a Brazilian state-owned gas firm.

The consortium, including Spain's Gas Natural SDG SA and Iberdrola SA, U.S. firm Enron Corp and Argentina's Pluspetrol Energy SA, paid a 74.8 percent premium on the minimum price of 355.8 million reais for both companies.
Spanish energy group Repsol owns 45 percent of Gas Natural SDG SA and Pluspetrol Energy SA.
"This is a fantastic result," said Rio state Finance Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar. "This exceeds our expectations. We were hoping for a premium of around 40 percent."
The CEG/Riogas sale is the third major privatization in Rio de Janeiro state, which has kept well ahead of other states in its privatization drive.
Last year, Rio state sold off its power firm Cerj, and only recently it became the first state to privatize its state-owned bank, Banerj.

Rio state sold off 56.4 percent of CEG's voting and total share capital for a minimum price of 250 million reais and 83.67 percent of Riogas' voting capital and 70.66 percent of Riogas preference shares for a base price of 105.8 million reais.

The winning consortium bid 464.2 million reais for CEG and 158 million reais for Riogas at the closed-envelope auction which took place on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange shortly after the state government managed to lift a court injunction blocking the sale.

The new owners plan to invest more than $150 million over the next five to six years in the two gas companies to expand the network and convert it from a manufactured gas network into a natural gas network.

"We want to develop a natural gas network that can satisfy levels of gas demand projected for the year 2000," Antoni Llarden, corporate director of industrial development at Gas Natural SDG SA, told reporters.

Llarden said the group expected the number of clients to increase by 600,000 in the next eight to 10 years from CEG's current 558,000 customers, turning CEG into one of few gas companies in the world that have more than one million clients.
No price hikes or job cuts are in the pipeline, he said.

Enron Corp now has a 25-percent stake in CEG, followed by Gas Natural with 19 percent, Iberdrola with 10 percent and Pluspetrol with two percent, while Riogas has been split between Gas Natural and Enron, with 51 percent and 32 percent of voting share capital, respectively.
